questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_104-->Surveys can provide invaluable insights, but only if they are ________ (would produce identical results if repeated) and ________ (actually measure what they are designed to measure).
<!--RsQ_105-->Pam needs to conduct primary research on the effects of networking in organizations. A ________ is suitable for this.
<!--RsQ_106-->________ surveys offer a number of advantages like speed, cost, and the ability to adapt the question set along the way based on a respondent's answers.
<!--RsQ_107-->________ reports provide the feedback that employees, managers, and others need in order to make decisions, take action, and respond to changes.
<!--RsQ_108-->When selecting people to participate in a survey, the most critical task is getting a ________ sample of the entire population in question.
<!--RsQ_109-->Sampling ________ can skew a survey by under- or overrepresenting certain segments of the population.
<!--RsQ_110-->Describe seven recommendations for effective surveys.

generalfeedback.text: 1. Provide clear instructions. 2. Don't ask questions that people cannot be expected to answer. 3. Keep the questionnaire short and easy to answer. Ask only relevant questions. Ideally, it should take less than 10-15 minutes to complete. 4. Develop questions that provide easy-to-analyse answers. Opinions are harder to analyse than numbers and facts. 5. Avoid leading questions. They will bias your survey. 6. Avoid ambiguous descriptions such as "often" or "frequently." 7. Ask only one thing at a time.

questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_111-->You are a customer in the luxury car market. Do you feel that your suggestions will be better received by the producers of these cars if they ask you to fill an online survey form, which declares that your feedback is valuable to the organization, or if somebody from the organization interviewed you face-to-face? Explain your answer.

generalfeedback.text: (Answers may vary.) Even though the online survey gives customers the option of giving their suggestions at their own convenience, the fact that the organization makes the effort to conduct a face-to-face interview and gather many more layers of information than an online survey would permit, would make the customer favour the interview over the online survey. Considering that there is a significant cost factor involved in conducting face-to-face interviews, customers may feel that the company is genuinely interested in their suggestions.

questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_112-->As part of your primary research, you are conducting a videotaped interview with a manager of a large retail store. After a few questions you notice that he is showing signs of impatience. How should you respond? What might you do differently to prevent this from happening in the future? Explain your answers.

generalfeedback.text:
(Answers may vary.) One of the possibilities is that the questions asked could be repetitive and don't require the expertise of the manager involved. To prevent this, you could place the questions in a careful sequence so that the potential answers could reveal layers of information.
It is also possible that, if it was a videotaped interview, the manager was not informed about this, until the interview. To prevent this, get people's permission before you videotape them. Additionally, the manager could also be pressed for time and hence get impatient. This can be avoided by always scheduling an appointment with the person concerned well in advance.

questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_130-->________ reports provide feedback on a wide variety of an organization's functions, including sales, inventories, expenses, shipments, and so on.
<!--RsQ_131-->________ reports range from brief descriptions of business procedures to manuals that run dozens or hundreds of pages.

<!--RsQ_132-->Ruth has to prepare an informational report, highlighting the disadvantages of an older approach and the advantages of a newer approach. The topical organization of her material would involve ________.
<!--RsQ_133-->Samantha needs to prepare and present a report that details the handling of certain hazardous materials in the organization's premises. For this she needs to prepare a ________ report.
<!--RsQ_134-->Website designers use the term ________ to describe the structure and navigational flow of all the parts of a website.
<!--RsQ_135-->In an informational report, ________ is the method of organizing the steps or stages in a process or procedure.
<!--RsQ_136-->In an informational report, ________ is the method of organizing a chain of events in order from oldest to newest or vice versa.
<!--RsQ_137-->In an informational report, ________ is the method of organizing by region, city, province or territory, country, or other geographic unit.
<!--RsQ_138-->In an informational report, ________ is the method of organizing by topical category, such as sales, profit, cost, or investment.
List and describe the four general categories of informational reports.

generalfeedback.text:
• Reports to monitor and control operations. Managers rely on a wide range of reports to see how well their companies are functioning. Plans establish expectations and guidelines to direct future action. Among the most important of these are business plans, which summarize a proposed business venture and describe the company's goals and plans for each major functional area. Operating reports provide feedback on a wide variety of an organization's functions, including sales, inventories, expenses, shipments, and so on. Personal activity reports provide information regarding individuals' experiences during sales calls, industry conferences, and other activities.
  • Reports to implement policies and procedures. Policy reports range from brief descriptions of business procedures to manuals that run dozens or hundreds of pages. Position papers, sometimes called white papers or backgrounders, outline an organization's official position on issues that affect the company's success.
  • Reports to demonstrate compliance. Businesses are required to submit a variety of compliance reports, from tax returns to reports describing the proper handling of hazardous materials.
  • Reports to document progress. Supervisors, investors, and customers frequently expect to be informed of the progress of projects and other activities. Progress reports range from simple updates in memo form to comprehensive status reports.

questiontext.text: Most informational reports use a topical organization. List five ways to organize materials and briefly describe each organizational strategy.

generalfeedback.text:
Any five of the following.

  • Comparison. Showing similarities and differences (or advantages and disadvantages) between two or more entities (refer to Figure 10.6).
  • Importance. Building up from the least important item to the most important (or from most important to the least, if you don't think your audience will read the entire report).
  • Sequence. Organizing the steps or stages in a process or procedure.
  • Chronology. Organizing a chain of events in order from oldest to newest or vice versa.
  • Geography. Organizing by region, city, province or territory, country, or other geographical unit.
  • Category. Grouping by topical category, such as sales, profit, cost, or investment.

questiontext.text: List three possible criteria for when you should use an infographic style of reporting.

generalfeedback.text:
Any three of the following.
Has to reach a wide audience

  • Is difficult to explain in words or could be communicated more clearly with visuals
  • Has data, especially significant data that you want to emphasize
  • Is significant enough to warrant the extra time for design and production
  • Is intended for distribution on social media

questiontext.text: List the tips involved in designing a website for business.

generalfeedback.text:
- If you know that a sizable percentage of your target audience will access your site with mobile devices, make sure the site is mobile friendly. Many contemporary blogging and website development platforms handle this for you.
- Give your readers control by creating links and pathways that let them explore on their own.
- Use simple, clear language for page titles and links so that visitors always know where they are and where a link will take them.
- Follow the conventions used by most business websites, such as having an "About Us" page that describes the company and a "Contact Us" page with phone, email, and messaging details.
- Help online readers scan and absorb information by breaking it into self-contained, easily readable chunks that are linked together logically. This is particularly helpful for mobile readers.

<!--RsQ_158-->After the substantial increases in productivity seen at their Oshawa plant, Delta Automobiles implemented similar upgrades at their Tampa plant. But the productivity at Tampa did not show any improvement. So the team that designed the upgrades was asked to prepare a troubleshooting report. What is the purpose of this troubleshooting report? Would a failure analysis report help in a similar situation and how? Which category of reports do both these reports belong to?

generalfeedback.text: The troubleshooting report would contain the analysis of the problem and possible solutions. Since the organization has not faced a similar situation in the past, a failure analysis report would not help in this matter. Both reports are analytical reports that help solve problems.

questiontext.text:
After a thorough analysis of the existing payroll management system, you have come up with multiple action points with details about where these changes should be implemented and by whom. In this analytical report, would you focus on conclusions or recommendations? Explain your answer.
Note that your action points could radically change the efficiency of the system, if implemented. However, since the changes are going to ruffle a time-tested system, they may be received with skepticism. If you sense that your readers will not receive these changes well, how would you modify your approach?

generalfeedback.text: The report specifically assigns tasks to its readers, so the report would focus on recommendations and not conclusions. If you feel that the readers may be hostile to these recommendations, you should use an indirect approach to logically put the points across.

<!--RsQ_178-->Why do unsolicited proposals offer more flexibility than solicited proposals? Can unsolicited proposals be sent within an organization? If yes, draft the introduction for one such unsolicited internal proposal. If not, explain your answer and draft an introduction for an unsolicited external proposal. Do proposals require secondary research and why?

generalfeedback.text:
(Answers may vary.) Unsolicited proposals offer more flexibility than solicited proposals because you do not have to restrict the proposal to the specifications mentioned in the RFP. Rather, you could use your resources and creativity to address a problem that the recipient may not be aware of and propose viable solutions.
Unsolicited internal proposals can be sent within an organization. The introduction for one such proposal would be as follows:
This team has been dedicated to the cause of helping this organization break new ground and create new markets. Most of this involves regular brainstorming and periodic meetings to collate ideas and create a plan of action. A lot of time could be saved if we have a preassigned meeting room for this purpose in our block-C and not waste time traveling to the next block to conduct our meetings. With minor changes to the now-defunct media room in our block, it can be converted to a much needed meeting room. Proposals require secondary research to identify viable solutions and to even quote sources. In the case of unsolicited proposals, secondary research can be used to identify potential clients.

<!--RsQ_034-->________ are customized online presentations of highly summarized business information.
<!--RsQ_035-->Describe the ways that analytical reports and proposals differ.

generalfeedback.text:
These two types of reports differ in terms of content and aims. Analytical reports offer information and analysis and can also include recommendations. These include reports to monitor and control operations, implement policies and procedures, demonstrate compliance, and document progress.
Proposals present persuasive recommendations to internal or external audiences, often involving investments or purchases. Proposals can be generated for internal needs or made to external agencies.

questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_036-->Briefly explain the primary function of a statement of purpose indicating the most useful way to phrase one. You have been asked to help a company find ways to reduce the amount it spends on employee health and dental benefits. Write a purpose statement for the report that you will produce.

generalfeedback.text:
(Answers may vary.) A statement of purpose defines why you are preparing your report and what you plan to deliver in the report. The most useful way to phrase your purpose statement is to begin with an infinitive phrase (to plus a verb), which helps pin down your general goal (to inform, to identify, to analyze, and so on).
The purpose statement to help a company find ways to reduce the amount it spends on employee health and dental benefits is "To identify ways to help reduce expenses on employee health and dental benefits."

questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_037-->Describe a work plan and list the elements a detailed work plan often contains.

generalfeedback.text:
For simpler reports, the work plan can be an informal list of tasks and a simple schedule. However, if you're preparing a lengthy report, particularly when you're collaborating with others, you will want to develop a more detailed work plan.
The elements in a detailed work-plan include:
- Statement of the problem
- Purpose and scope of work
- Sources and methods of data collection
- Preliminary Outline
- Task assignments and schedule

questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_038-->List and describe the five elements that usually are part of a formal work plan.

generalfeedback.text: (Answers may vary.) 1. Statement of the problem: This clarifies the problem you are addressing and helps you stay focused on the goal. 2. Purpose and scope of your investigation: This describes what you plan to accomplish and the boundaries of your work. It states what you will and will not cover. 3. Sources and methods of data collection. 4. Preliminary outline. 5. List of tasks to be accomplished: List the things to do, the amount of time needed for each task, the research necessary, and any constraints.

<!--RsQ_064-->As a researcher, evaluating the sources of information carefully is vital because wrong information makes you lose credibility and taints your reputation. What points should you keep in mind while evaluating the validity of your information? If you quote information from a secondary research source, such as Wikipedia, and credit the source, would your information be considered credible? Explain your answer.

generalfeedback.text:
The points to keep in mind when evaluating a source are:
- Reliability of the source
- Point of view of the source (biased/unbiased)
- Purpose of the material
- Author credibility
- Reference used by the source
- Is the material independently verifiable?
- Is the material current and complete?
- Does the information make sense?
Quoting information from a source such as Wikipedia is not usually preferable because most of the pages contain errors, and the fact that anyone, experts or not, can edit the pages, makes it unreliable.

questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_065-->What is the difference between quoting, paraphrasing, and summarizing? When would you use each in a report?

generalfeedback.text:
You can use textual information from secondary sources in three ways.
Quoting a source means you reproduce the material exactly as you found it (giving full credit to the source, of course). Use direct quotations when the original language will enhance your argument or when rewording the passage would reduce its impact. However, be careful with direct quotes: using too many creates a choppy patchwork of varying styles and gives the impression that all you've done is piece together the work of other people. When quoting sources, set off shorter passages with quotation marks and set off longer passages (generally five lines or more) as separate, indented paragraphs.
You can often maximize the impact of secondary material in your own writing by paraphrasing it: restating it in your own words and with your own sentence structures. Paraphrasing helps you maintain consistent tone while using vocabulary that's familiar to your audience. Of course, you still need to credit the originator of the information (by citing the source), but you don't need quotation marks or indented paragraphs.
Summarizing is similar to paraphrasing but presents the gist of the material in fewer words than the original by leaving out details, examples, and less important information. Summarizing is not always a simple task, and your audience will judge your ability to separate significant issues from less significant details. Like quotations and paraphrases, summaries also require complete documentation of sources.
Of course, all three approaches require careful attention to ethics. When quoting directly, take care not to distort the original intent of the material by quoting selectively.

questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_079-->Powerful search tools include ________ search engines that search all the computers on a company's network.

<!--RsQ_081-->Internet research tools fall into two categories: search tools and ________ tools.

<!--RsQ_083-->________ use human editors to categorize and evaluate websites.
<!--RsQ_084-->Explain the difference between primary and secondary information.

generalfeedback.text: Primary information comes directly from an original source. You might look at an original document such as a sales report, a memo, or a balance sheet, or talk with an expert in the field or with someone who has direct experience with your issue. For secondary information, you usually go to the library or visit a website. There you look for information that a writer has produced on your subject.

questiontext.text: <!--RsQ_085-->Explain the five suggestions for effectively conducting database searches.

generalfeedback.text: 1. Read instructions and pay attention to the details. 2. Review the search and display options carefully so you don't misinterpret the results. 3. Try variations of your terms. 4. Use fewer search terms to find more results; use more terms to find fewer results. 5. Look beyond the first page results.

questiontext.text: Explain why you should reference borrowed information. Discuss 3-5 reasons. Explain when you should reference borrowed information and what kind of information needs to be referenced. Discuss research tips.

generalfeedback.text:
You should reference borrowed material in order to avoid plagiarism; however, there are other reasons as well:

  • it properly and ethically credits the person who created the original material
  • it shows your audience that you have sufficient support for your message
  • it helps readers explore your topic in more detail if they choose.

Whatever method you choose, documentation is necessary for website material, books, articles, tables, charts, diagrams, song lyrics, scripted dialogue, letters, speeches-anything that you take from someone else, including ideas and information that you've re-expressed through paraphrasing or summarizing. However, you do not have to cite a source for knowledge that's generally known among your readers.
When researching, be sure to start with secondary research and then fill in the gaps with primary research. Take detailed notes and keep copies of your source materials. Avoid using large chunks of borrowed material and simply cutting and pasting sources together. Instead, use research to support your ideas and give credibility to your position. Also, be sure to integrate borrowed information into your writing and use a variety of methods, such as quoting, paraphrasing, and summarizing.
